title: How many whole units are there in seven halves?
description: Seven halves is split into pairs of halves that make whole units. The board counts the pairs, keeps the half that is left and checks by putting the pieces back together.
teaching_notes: One idea: each pair of halves is one whole unit, and a single half cannot make another. Watch for students who count the halves as whole units.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (section 7.5, first block), Math Talk
video_script.why: A learner finds the whole units in a fraction greater than one by grouping its halves in twos.
video_script.substitution: the book's own fraction seven halves
video_script.anchor: seven half-unit bars in a row
video_script.payoff_line: There are three whole units in seven halves

final_answer.spoken: three whole units, with one half left over

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, six halves, seven halves
maths_rules: 7/2 means 7 parts, each 1/2 of a unit
2 halves make 1 whole, so 6 halves make 3 wholes
video_script.design: Seven half bars in a row. They join in pairs into three whole bars and one half stays alone.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; seven half-unit bars in a row; the fraction 7/2 written beside them

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.bars: seven half-unit bars line up in a row
marks.ask: the fraction seven halves is written beside the bars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about halves.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>Seven half bars are lined up in a row.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many whole units are there in seven halves?

beats.on_screen: the bars and the fraction stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a whole unit bar beside two half bars of the same total length

marks.whole: a whole unit bar appears beside two half bars of the same length

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Two halves put together are the same length as one whole unit.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fraction that we have to look at is seven halves.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many whole units are in 7/2
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many whole units are in seven halves.

marks.split: seven halves is written as seven halves added together

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, we use the same way as the example in your book. Write seven halves as seven halves added together.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 2 halves = 1 whole, so 6 halves = 3 wholes

marks.pairs: the halves join in pairs and three whole bars form

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step two, two halves make one whole. Six halves make three wholes, because there are three pairs.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 7 halves = 6 halves + 1 half, so 1 half is left over

marks.left: the seventh half bar stays alone after the three whole bars

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, seven halves is six halves and one more half. That one half is left over.

beats.on_screen: Check: 3 wholes = 6 halves, and 6 halves + 1 half = 7 halves

marks.check: the three wholes and the left over half are put back together as seven halves

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, put the pieces back together. Six halves and one half make seven halves again.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>There are three whole units in seven halves.
It also has one more half left over.
